searchText: Finally now I'm looking into this. One thing to note is that two ILs with the same content but different transactions order have different signatures. Given that we're broadcasting signed ILs, I think it's easier and better to just consider them as equivocation, without looking into their content to compare transaction bytes by bytes. What do you think? Stream: https://youtube.com/watch?v=Ga8Hpx1tHb8 https://x.com/i/broadcasts/1ynJOMrmeMZKR Yea that makes sense EL clients, if you have any issues on counting the total number of valid/invalid IL transactions, please, let me know. We're currently discussing this list of metrics: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-metrics/pull/4#discussion_r2406702189 Was there a link to the L2 FOCIL website? > yes: one assumption that rollups *do not make* on L1 is that an attacker holds < 50% of the stake. And it makes sense not to make this assumption because the rollup bridge may contain more than that value. FOCIL would be fantastic to guarantee censor resistance in less than a challenge period without this assumption, but unfortunately it needs it <@755590043632140352> I guess the stake means the staked tokens in a rollup contract? What happens when an attacker holds >50% of the stake? https://native-rollups.l2beat.com/forced_transactions.html In FOCIL, if the attacker holds more than 50% of the stake, you can always pretend that you didn't see the includer's ILs and prevent the whole mechanism of working as intended this is not something inherently bad from FOCIL, it's just the way it is with anything that is enforced off-chain But the point is that it doesn't allow rollups to assume that there won't be censorship in any time window because they don't want to make the assumption about 50% of stake being honest, rightfully so Right, so it's staked ETH in L1. Having control over >50% of total stake sounds like very strong attack, but it's always good to know which trust assumptions it's based on Ethereum does have this security: even if an attacker has 100% of the stake, they cannot finalize an invalid block. For L2s this is not the case if their censoring mechanism requires an assumption on minimal honesty for stakers. An attacker that manages to censor for over enough time can post an invalid state transition on L2 Here is the amd64 Reth image `pellekrab/reth-focil:a2306c6` Does it make sense to put higher threshold like 75% or whatnot? Or what about putting some limit on which value the rollup bridge can have value up to? no, this is a fundamental issue about offchain validation, which is the strength of FOCIL Got what you mean, thanks!
